--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "General cooperation advice says consider mutual cooperation, but objective maximize."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates first, retaliates against defections, forgives isolated defections, and defects against always-defectors. Simulated against population strategies (TFT, grim, all-C, all-D, endgame exploiters) and identified bugs (final-round defect never triggers, all-C not exploited). Changed by fixing final round to defect, considering endgame exploitation, and evaluating probing for pure cooperators.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says 'Avoid allowing an isolated defection to cause permanent mutual retaliation' and 'Consider forgiveness after a temporary disruption'."
STRATEGY: Parent is a mostly-cooperative conditional strategy that punishes single defections once, forgives after its own punishment, and randomly defects in the last five rounds. The trace simulates it against slot5 (mostly C with 5% random D) and against TFT/endgame exploiters, then proposes a revised strategy: forgive rare defections immediately, defect on the final round, and exploit opponents whose defection rate exceeds 50%.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the forgiveness rule based on overall defection rate <=10% seems reasonable. Let's keep it."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates, punishes consecutive defections, forgives single defections based on overall defection rate, and defects on the final round. The trace simulates this against TFT, Grim, pure C, always-D, slot4 (endgame exploiter), slot5 (random defector), slot7, slot9, and slot10. It adds an endgame override to punish defections at n>=98, and considers probing/exploiting opponents who defected first.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent does this: if last == 'D', it punishes." / "The parent doesn't do this; it mostly cooperates." / "The parent already has a probe in endgame: if op_c*5 >= n*4 and n>=95, 25% chance D."
STRATEGY: Parent punishes a defection once, then returns to cooperation, with an endgame probe against very cooperative opponents. The trace simulates the parent against slot5, slot7, slot9, TFT, grim, all-C, and all-D. It changes the parent by adding a learning/exploit loop: defect again when the opponent cooperated after our defection, cooperate when they retaliated, punish when they defect first, and probe with 20% (or 5% if we have defected) when both cooperated.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent had a condition: if op_c*5 >= n*4 and n>=95, 25% D. That applies when op_d is small but not necessarily 0." / "The parent does: if op_c*5 >= n*4 and n>=95, 25% D. We could keep that."
STRATEGY: Parent is a cooperative/punishing strategy with an endgame defect and a late-game random probe; the trace simulates it against Always Defect, All-C, TFT, Grim, and slot5/slot7-style opponents; it revises by adding an exploit loop after opponent-first defection, an op_d*2>n always-defect rule, and a stronger n>=95 punishment rule.
